reason: Self-driving DBMS behaviour-model training-data collection is ML-for-DBMS rather than OS resource management; PostgreSQL single-node runs fit but repo completeness is unknown.
Static bug detection is program analysis, not resource management, though the explicit analysis-time/bugs-found knob is a clean improvement target and everything is CPU-only user space.

VM rescheduling is a genuine resource-management problem and the whole evaluation is a trace-driven simulator plus a small policy net, so it fits the machine exactly; only trace availability is uncertain.
An LSH-based approximate cache in front of RAG is a textbook admission/eviction/approximation policy study on one GPU; only risk is a multi-tens-of-GB corpus download and a user-space Rust install.
Excellent badged artifact and CPU-only, but privacy static analysis is far from OS resource management and the result is fairly closed to incremental systems extension.
Upgrade fuzzing of distributed storage is testing rather than storage-engine design, and each campaign is expensive even collapsed to local multi-process clusters.
Core LLM-serving kernel work (prefill/decode overlap) that is single-GPU and FA2-style so Ampere is fine; main risk is building the vAttention CUDA stack on driver 535.
Buffer virtualization is squarely a memory topic, but it relies on explicit huge pages which need root here and no repository was located.
DBMS knob tuning is only systems-adjacent and no code release was found, so the artifact would have to be rebuilt from the paper.
Operator synthesis is an ML-compiler topic with a linked main repo plus separate artifact repo; single-GPU search fits but search compute is the budget risk.
User-space virtual memory paging working sets to NVMe is exactly the memory topic, but MPC parties must be collapsed to co-located processes and the 2026 repo's maturity is unknown.
A learned spatial-keyword index is a narrow learned-index result with no official code found, so there is little to build on.
Self-contained streaming float compression codec runs trivially on CPU and invites clear policy/encoding variants; repo is linked but a brand-new 2026 release of unknown completeness.
DNN verification of learned system agents is analysis/verification rather than resource management, and Marabou-style queries scale poorly on 16 cores.
KV-cache management policy inside an inference engine is the ideal topic and fits one GPU with a small model; the 2026 repo's completeness is unverified.
LLM-driven engine synthesis is a data-systems/LLM result that needs paid API budget and long synthesis loops, making a 10-week improvement costly.
Makespan scheduling for multi-LLM jobs is on-topic and the released simulator is usable, but the GPU-allocation half assumes several GPUs so only a scaled-down slice reproduces.
Accuracy-aware compilation offers many tunable knobs, but it is compiler work and requires a from-source LLVM/MLIR build in $HOME, which is a large fraction of the budget.
Pure CPU C++ compression layout with an active repo; the AVX2-only Zen3 target means headline numbers will not reproduce, which is itself a testable scale-down hypothesis.
Only the solver/simulation half survives without the 4xGH200 testbed, and cross-datacenter pipeline training is far from a single-machine OS problem.
Learned space-filling-curve layout is a narrow data-layout result and no repository was located.
Plain-C single-machine log compression plus query engine with an explicit artifact statement and an active repo; only the Alibaba log datasets may need substitution.
A user-space recovery dry-run runtime is systems-adjacent and runnable as local processes, but some case studies assume production scale and the 2026 repo is unproven.
FUSE-based fail-slow injection is usable here, but the harness ships CloudLab/Ansible/Docker deployment for six normally multi-node systems, so nearly everything must be re-plumbed.
Cost models and caching over a model zoo are systems-adjacent, but the full zoo plus datasets is a large download against ~257 GB free.
Carbon-aware batch scheduling with a released Zenodo artifact whose pure-simulation interface reproduces most figures on one machine; policy swaps are easy to phrase as hypotheses.
Shared input pipelines target a real CPU-side I/O bottleneck and collocation is demonstrable on one GPU; the interconnect-dependent parts scale down but the repo's completeness is unknown.
Self-contained user-space C++ compression with TPC-C evaluation runs entirely on CPU and offers obvious encoder/model variants to test.
Trivially runnable pure-Python runtime rewriter, but dynamic pandas rewriting is a language-runtime optimization rather than an OS resource-management problem.
Single-GPU ML compiler work, but the artifact is upstream Apache TVM, a huge fast-moving codebase where isolating and improving the paper's contribution is hard.

Zero-copy splice-based data delivery between Wasm functions is a genuine I/O-path mechanism with local microbenchmarks, but the artifact assumes containerd/OCI packaging that is unavailable without Docker or root.

AE Available+Functional, pure user-space Python tuner needing only timers; the different noise profile of this shared machine is itself a ready-made testable hypothesis, though tuning is systems-adjacent.
Workload-aware GPU-memory caching and CPU-GPU-disk coordination is explicitly designed for limited GPU memory, so an A5000 is the right target; repo completeness is unverified.
A learned component inside a tensor compiler is on the edge of scope and fine-tuning the model is compute-heavy, so the project would depend on released checkpoints.
Commit/logging protocol design against NVMe parallelism is core storage-engine work that this machine's two NVMe devices can host; LeanStore research branches are the build risk.
User-space heartbeat scheduling for multicore parallelism suits a 16C/32T machine, but the LLVM/NOELLE toolchain build plus the signal/timer rollforward path is a heavy lift.
AE-reviewed single-GPU artifact with an accuracy/speed knob, but declarative video analytics is an application-level ML-systems topic.
No official repo found and the Legion evaluation targets supercomputers, so both the artifact and the scale are missing.
Badged, CPU-only, fully simulated scheduler that fits perfectly, but with no systems-engineering slack any improvement must come purely from a better knapsack heuristic.
Runs as local JVM processes and state-space exploration time is a clear improvement target, but model-checking-guided testing is outside the resource-management core.
Single-GPU temporal-GNN framework is a legitimate ML-systems artifact, but it is a domain-specific runtime with limited OS-resource angle.
A 10,000-GPU-hour design-space study is mainly ML modeling and only a small slice of the space is affordable in 10 weeks on one A5000.
Spilling and out-of-memory operators on NVMe is excellent OS-topic material, but no repository was found and the paper assumes a larger NVMe array.
A multi-layer embedding cache on a single node is a clean admission/eviction policy playground with many obvious policy swaps; only artifact maturity is unclear.
Runs trivially on CPU SIMD with a maintained repo, but vector quantization for ANN is an algorithmic result with little OS resource-management content.
Membership filters with explicit LSM/storage use cases are CPU-only and cheap to experiment with; composition choices give many testable variants.
Microbatched imputation inside a research DBMS kernel is a narrow data-systems contribution with modest extension space.
LLM-guided knob tuning has no located repo and needs an external LLM endpoint plus long tuning loops.
The optimizer is user-space Python, but the premise is a heterogeneous geo-distributed multi-region GPU cluster, so only a fully simulated stand-in is possible.
Single-machine memory-bound C++ with a real repo, but cross-modal ANN graph indexing sits at the edge of the storage topic.
CPU-only and would fit the machine, but no repo was found and it is not in the AE results list, so there is nothing to build upon.
Trace-driven burst/stable write separation is a real storage I/O-path policy, but the code has no README or build instructions, the paper is paywalled, and the multi-role system must be co-located.
Learned lifetime prediction for log-structured data placement with a CPU simulator and an oracle baseline is an ideal hypothesis target; only the ZNS prototype half is out of reach.

Fluctuation-aware cache plus IOPS allocator in a RocksDB derivative is prime OS material with many policy knobs, but reproducing the EBS latency premise needs a FUSE or injection shim and the badge is Available only.
The hash-table design is in-topic, but the headline results and the libpmem-linked build target Optane PMEM that this machine lacks, leaving only the DRAM configuration.
I/O-aware hierarchical index building profiles the local NVMe entirely in user space, and the storage-profile-driven tuning invites clean incremental variants.
Placement learning over synthetic graphs in a simulator runs easily here, but simulator fidelity undercuts any improvement claim and placement is only loosely an OS topic.
Holistic RL DBMS tuning is ML-for-databases and the tuning runs are long enough to consume most of a 10-week budget.
The sparse-kernel mechanism is per-GPU and Ampere-compatible, but the AE asks for 8xV100 or A100-80GB and 200-700 GB disk and ships as Docker, so both scale-down and a conda port are required.
Compression with direct query-on-compressed-data is on-topic storage work on a single-node JVM system; Java must be installed in user space and repo maturity is unknown.
An LSM-tree whose compaction transforms layout is core storage-engine work on a single node; the research repo's build quality is the main unknown.
Sparse-format search is an ML-compiler artifact whose single-Ampere-GPU setting matches this machine, but it is far from resource management.
Memory planning and quantization workflows are interesting, but the evaluation targets phones/NPUs/MCUs that are unavailable and the artifact is a very large fast-moving upstream project.
LLM placement and request scheduling is exactly the target topic and the released cluster simulator fits one machine, but the real-hardware results need 24-42 heterogeneous GPUs.
Ideal topic on paper, but no code was found and the target is a multi-instance serving cluster, so everything would have to be reimplemented from scratch.
LLM-discovered LLVM peephole rewrites verified by Alive2 is compiler research with essentially no OS resource-management content, and it needs an LLM API budget.
A semantics-aware LSM key-value store on single-node NVMe is squarely in the storage topic; the Ethereum state workload has to be sourced and the repo is unverified.
Maintained, tiny Python package with an obvious space of regressor improvements, but its exploration loop invokes real AWS Lambda, which this single-machine environment cannot provide.
An adaptive range filter would be a perfect small CPU-only project, but no public repository was located so the artifact would have to be written from the paper.
CPU-only artifact explicitly targeting 16 physical cores, but speculative Protobuf parsing is a parsing/compiler topic rather than resource management.
Learned index-benefit estimation is ML-for-databases with no repo or even abstract located and a possible commercial-engine target.
Best Paper with a Distinguished Artifact whose only system requirement is FUSE, which this machine has; a user-space file system is a core OS topic and only the LLM API key/spend is a real cost.
CPU-only OpenMP C++ that builds and runs in user space on 16 cores with a clear speedup metric, but the domain is PGM inference rather than OS resource management.
The plain multi-threaded CPU variant suits 16 cores and multicore aggregation offers real tuning headroom, but the DPDK/XDP paths are blocked and CAIDA traces must be sourced separately.
Fairness/efficiency cluster scheduling with a trace-driven discrete-event simulator that runs entirely on CPU is an excellent policy-swap target; only the physical-cluster arm is out of reach.
Training-set construction for learned DBMS components is off the OS core and no artifact was found in search.

Fine-grained GPU sharing by intercepting kernel launches in user space is single-GPU by design and contention-focused, giving many scheduling-policy hypotheses; the pinned PyTorch/CUDA toolchain on driver 535 is the main risk.
Disk-resident graph layout optimized for I/O reduction is real storage locality work on local NVMe, though it straddles the storage/vector-index boundary and repo maturity is unknown.
In-memory multicore concurrency in user-space C++ runs perfectly here, but a concurrent search tree is a data-structure result rather than an OS resource-management system.
A reusable benchmark harness over learned indexes would be easy to extend, but the artifact URL was not located and the paper is an experiments-and-analysis study rather than a system.
